title: The Pound drifts lower as the Fed lines up a rate above the Bank of England's
body: GBP/USD closed Tuesday near 1.3470, down 0.2%. Wednesday's Asian and London hours are the last before the Fed is expected to raise its rate for the first time since July 2023. By the New York close its ceiling should sit a quarter-point above Bank Rate.

title: US Crude Stocks Surge
body: US crude oil inventories surged by 7.14 million barrels in the week ending September 11, reversing a decline of 300,000 barrels in the prior week. Over the past 22 weeks, commercial crude inventories excluding the Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) have fallen by slightly more than 41 million barrels, even as total US crude inventories have risen by nearly 10 million barrels since the start of the year. During the same week, an additional 400,000 barrels were released from the SPR, reducing its total holdings to 285 million barrels. The SPR's generally accepted operational minimum is estimated at 250–300 million barrels. At Cushing, Oklahoma, inventories declined by 246,000 barrels, following a 300,000-barrel draw in the previous week. US crude production increased to 13.947 million barrels per day in the week ending September 4, up from 13.862 million barrels per day a week earlier. On the refined products side, gasoline inventories rose by 1.46 million barrels, while distillate stocks climbed by 1.61 million barrels. title: New Zealand Consumer Mood Brightens as Westpac Sentiment Jumps in Q3 2026
body: New Zealand consumer confidence strengthened notably in the third quarter of 2026, according to the latest Westpac Consumer Sentiment data released on 15 September 2026. The index rose to 89.5 in Q3, up from 80.4 in the second quarter of 2026. While the headline figure remains below the 100-point threshold that typically separates pessimism from optimism, the near nine-point jump suggests a meaningful improvement in households' outlook compared with earlier in the year. The gain indicates that New Zealand consumers are feeling less downbeat about their financial position and the broader economic environment than they were in the second quarter. The Q3 2026 reading will be closely watched by markets and policymakers as a potential signal of shifting momentum in domestic demand. A sustained recovery in consumer sentiment is often seen as a precursor to firmer household spending, a key driver of New Zealand's economic performance. title: Uruguay Economy Shrinks in Q2 2026
body: Uruguay's GDP fell 0.5% year over year in the second quarter of 2026. Output in agriculture, fisheries, and mining contracted 22.2%, reflecting a weak soybean harvest in the 2025/2026 season caused by drought, as well as an unfavorable comparison with the prior season, which had delivered historically high yields. Manufacturing expanded 1.9%, supported by increased cellulose pulp production. Activity in trade, accommodation, and food and beverage services rose 2.8%, driven primarily by robust performance in the trade sector. Construction grew 4.2%, underpinned by higher investment in both nonresidential buildings and other construction projects. The material has been provided by InstaForex Company - www.instaforex.com

title: Ibovespa Rises on Energy and Finance Gains
body: The Ibovespa advanced 0.5% on Tuesday, closing at 186,503 points, driven mainly by Petrobras and major financial stocks. Petrobras climbed 3.1% as oil prices extended their rally, amid supply disruptions in the Middle East after Saudi Arabia shut down a key pipeline bypassing the Strait of Hormuz on Monday. On the monetary policy front, investors expect the Selic easing cycle to continue at Wednesday's meeting, with the benchmark rate projected to be cut to 13.75% from 14%, as recent inflation readings have remained within the BCB's tolerance range. Among financials, Itaú and Itaúsa both added 0.8%, while BB Seguridade advanced 1%. In the steel sector, Gerdau rose 3.1% and Usiminas 3.3% after Safra initiated a long-short recommendation, suggesting a long position in Gerdau and a short position in Usiminas. Gerdau was also named one of the world's most trusted companies in the "World's Most Trustworthy Companies 2026" ranking for the fourth consecutive year. title: U.S. API Crude Inventories Swing to Sharp Build, Surging 7.14M Barrels
body: U.S. crude oil stockpiles recorded a steep increase in the latest week, with American Petroleum Institute (API) data showing inventories rose by 7.14 million barrels, compared with a marginal draw of 0.30 million barrels previously. The updated figure, released on 15 September 2026, marks a notable reversal in the weekly trend. The move from a small decline to a sizeable build suggests a significant shift in the balance between supply and demand over the latest reporting period. Market participants will be watching how this data aligns with upcoming official government inventory figures, as the scale of the build could influence short-term sentiment in the oil market and expectations for U.S. production and refinery activity. Traders and analysts are likely to assess whether the surge reflects softer domestic consumption, higher imports, or changes in refinery runs, as the sudden inventory jump may feed into price volatility in the near term. title: TSX Slips as Bond Yields Rise
body: The S&P/TSX Composite Index slipped 0.3% to close at 35,582 on Tuesday, pressured by surging oil prices and elevated bond yields. Yields on 10-year Canadian government bonds moved toward the 4% mark, hovering near their highest levels since 2007. The prospect of higher interest rates weighed on rate-sensitive sectors ahead of the U.S. Federal Reserve's expected 25-basis-point policy rate hike on Wednesday. Financials finished lower, with TD Bank down 0.5%, CIBC off 0.6%, and National Bank declining 1.3%. The mining sector also ended mostly in the red, dragged by softer gold prices. Retailers recorded steep losses, as Alimentation Couche-Tard (ATD) fell 2.7% and Loblaw dropped 2.3%. Meanwhile, Prime Minister Mark Carney announced immediate tax write-offs for most new capital investments, aiming to stimulate economic growth and draw in foreign capital. Carney is hosting dozens of global investors in Toronto this week to promote investment in strategic projects, against the backdrop of ongoing trade tensions with the United States. title: US Stocks Drop as Yields Extend Surge
body: US stock indices closed lower on Tuesday, pressured by a renewed surge in bond yields. The S&P 500 slipped 0.4%, the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 328 points, and the Nasdaq Composite declined 0.6%. The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield climbed to its highest level in nearly two decades. Intensifying strikes in the Middle East further clouded the outlook for regional energy supplies, heightening inflation risks and reinforcing expectations of a more hawkish Federal Reserve. With higher fuel costs contributing to this year's inflationary pressures, markets are pricing in a 25 bp rate hike at tomorrow's Fed meeting. Losses were broad-based, with credit-sensitive AI hyperscalers coming under pressure from rising borrowing costs. Alphabet fell 1.3%, Microsoft lost 1.6%, Oracle dropped 3.1%, and Amazon declined 2%. By contrast, chipmakers mostly rebounded after Monday's selloff, triggered in part by Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei's call to slow AI development to address risks from increasingly powerful models. Nvidia gained 0.6%, while AMD advanced 2.2%. The material has been provided by InstaForex Company - www.instaforex.com

title: Oil Rally Intensifies on Middle East Risks
body: Crude oil climbed above $105.50 a barrel on Tuesday, its highest level in four months, after Saudi Arabia reportedly cancelled several shipments following drone attacks that forced the shutdown of a key export pipeline. The kingdom is said to have informed some European customers that certain September deliveries would be cancelled, while crude loadings at the Red Sea port of Yanbu were suspended. At the same time, Iran-backed Houthi militants resumed strikes on Saudi targets this week, adding to regional tensions. Security in the Strait of Hormuz remains fragile, with at least two tankers attacked since Saturday. According to data from Kpler, commodity vessel traffic through the strait dropped to four ships on Monday, down from 10 the previous day. Disruptions extended beyond the Gulf. In Libya, the national oil company halted production at two oilfields and a pumping station amid ongoing protests. In Eastern Europe, Russia struck petrol stations in Kyiv, while Ukraine targeted a Russian oil refinery, despite US President Donald Trump's announcement that both sides had agreed to cease attacks on each other's energy infrastructure.
